key_insight: Atomically engineered LaVO3/PrVO3 superlattices enable composition-dependent tuning of antiferromagnetic ordering alongside controlled structural distortions.
engineering_relevance: Layer-by-layer oxide growth offers a route to tailoring magnetic properties through strain and interface design; the abstract does not report AI methods or solar-cell applications.
method: Grow LaVO3/PrVO3 superlattices by molecular beam epitaxy on (001) SrTiO3.
Characterize epitaxial strain and crystal quality using X-ray diffraction and reciprocal space mapping.
Map atomic displacements and orbital hybridization using high-resolution STEM and layer-resolved spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a single tunable antiferromagnetic transition, periodicity-dependent antipolar displacements, and interface-suppressed distortions that recover over a few unit cells.
watch_item: Trilinear structural coupling is inferred indirectly from displacement and hybridization proxies, and the abstract provides no quantitative tuning range.
